newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Vienna stocks slip as futures expire.
newsitem.headline: Vienna stocks slip as futures expire.

text.p: Austrian stocks ended lower on Friday, although up three percent on the week and traders expect the market to trade with a firm bias next week as well.
The ATX index of 21 blue chips lost 6.01 points, or 0.57 percent, to close at 1,039.53 with just two shares gaining, 16 falling and three unchanged.
Traders said the market was pressured lower late in the session by players squaring off positions ahead of the weekend.
"In the morning, we thought we could take advantage of the strong international leads," said one trader.

"It's a pity that we've again closed below 1,040," said another trader, in reference to the six-week long efforts to break out of the 1,020 to 1,040-point range. On Thursday, the ATX managed to close above 1,040.
Die Erste savings bank expects a firm market next week. Once the break-out above 1,040 points is confirmed, the next targets are 1,070 to 1,080. Die Erste recommends buying Radex and VA Stahl.
Creditanstalt is also sanguine, citing the Vienna market's room for catch-up compared with international markets. Its recommendations remain VA Tech and VAE, with OMV interesting as a cyclical play.
But a senior trader at a major bank cited caution. "There's too much selling interest in certain issues for my liking. And I doubt that it can be fully absorbed."
The day's leading gainer was VA Stahl, up 1.86 percent at 356.5, while Wolford was the top loser, shedding 2.86 percent to 2,750.
The new benchmark October ATX future fell three points to 1,047 on turnover of 910 contracts.
The all-share Vienna bourse index fell 0.38 percent to 404.7 points.
